summary.en: Solve reaching definitions and live variables with explicit GEN, KILL, USE, DEF sets and synchronous fixed-point rounds.
summary.bn: কোন মান কোথা থেকে আসতে পারে আর পরে কোথায় লাগবে, তা তুমি ব্লকের সেট আপডেট করে বের করবে।

notes: Python programs use the standard library and were executed with Python 3.12.14.

practice.title: Build local definition sets
practice.statementHtml: For the diamond graph, compute every GEN and KILL set and explain why KILL refers to other definitions of assigned variables.
hints: Definition labels identify assignments, not names.
practice.answerHtml:
Use the following graph. The test choosing B1 or B2 uses an external flag, which is not among the variables analysed below. Definition labels name individual assignments, not variable names. B3 returns z after computing it.

Blocks and local statements
BlockStatementsSuccessors
B0d1: x=1; d2: y=2B1,B2
B1d3: x=y+1B3
B2d4: y=x+2B3
B3d5: z=x+y; return zexit

For reaching definitions, a definition reaches a point if some path brings it there without another assignment to the same variable. GEN[B] contains definitions from B that survive to its exit. KILL[B] contains other definitions of variables assigned in B. If a block assigns x twice, only the final assignment to x belongs in GEN.

Complete GEN and KILL sets for the diamond
BlockGENKILLPredecessors
B0{d1,d2}{d3,d4}none
B1{d3}{d1}B0
B2{d4}{d2}B0
B3{d5}{}B1,B2

The forward equations are IN[B] = union of OUT[P] over predecessors P, and OUT[B] = GEN[B] union (IN[B] minus KILL[B]). Set the entry boundary to empty because this example has no incoming definitions for x, y or z. A language with parameters could model their entry definitions explicitly.

practice.title: Solve reaching definitions
practice.statementHtml: Show all synchronous reaching-definition rounds for the four-block diamond from empty sets.
hints: A round reads the preceding round of neighbour facts.
practice.answerHtml:
Initialise every IN and OUT to empty. The following table uses synchronous rounds: all new IN values read the preceding round's OUT values. OUT is then computed from that round's new IN. A different worklist order may reach the same fixed point in fewer visible steps.

Complete reaching-definition iteration, each cell is IN / OUT
RoundB0B1B2B3
0{} / {}{} / {}{} / {}{} / {}
1{} / {d1,d2}{} / {d3}{} / {d4}{} / {d5}
2{} / {d1,d2}{d1,d2} / {d2,d3}{d1,d2} / {d1,d4}{d3,d4} / {d3,d4,d5}
3{} / {d1,d2}{d1,d2} / {d2,d3}{d1,d2} / {d1,d4}{d1,d2,d3,d4} / {d1,d2,d3,d4,d5}
4{} / {d1,d2}{d1,d2} / {d2,d3}{d1,d2} / {d1,d4}{d1,d2,d3,d4} / {d1,d2,d3,d4,d5}

At B3 entry, both definitions of x and both definitions of y may reach. This does not mean four assignments execute together on one incoming path. B1 supplies d3 with d2, while B2 supplies d1 with d4. The set abstraction intentionally forgets that correlation, which makes it safe but sometimes imprecise.

practice.title: Solve liveness
practice.statementHtml: Compute USE, DEF and all live-variable rounds for the diamond, explaining why z is absent from B3 USE.
hints: A read after a local definition does not require an incoming value.
practice.answerHtml:
A variable is live at a point when some path uses its current value before redefining it. USE[B] lists variables read before any local definition. DEF[B] lists variables assigned in B. The return z in B3 does not put z in USE[B3], because B3 defines z before reading it.

Complete USE and DEF sets
BlockUSEDEFExplanation
B0{}{x,y}Both right sides are constants
B1{y}{x}Read incoming y before assigning x
B2{x}{y}Read incoming x before assigning y
B3{x,y}{z}x,y feed z; return uses locally defined z

The backward equations are OUT[B] = union of IN[S] over successors S, and IN[B] = USE[B] union (OUT[B] minus DEF[B]). Give the exit an empty live set here, because return has already been represented inside B3. External observable memory would need an appropriate boundary or effect model.

Complete live-variable rounds, each cell is IN / OUT
RoundB0B1B2B3
0{} / {}{} / {}{} / {}{} / {}
1{} / {}{y} / {}{x} / {}{x,y} / {}
2{} / {x,y}{y} / {x,y}{x} / {x,y}{x,y} / {}
3{} / {x,y}{y} / {x,y}{x} / {x,y}{x,y} / {}

Read B1 carefully. Its outgoing x is live because B3 uses the x assigned by B1. Its incoming x is not live because B1 replaces x before that future use. Incoming y remains live because the assignment x=y+1 reads it immediately.

practice.title: Propagate through a loop
practice.statementHtml: Solve reaching definitions for L0 initialisation, self-looping L1 updates and L2 return.
hints: Initial and previous-iteration definitions can both enter L1.
practice.answerHtml:
Now use L0: d1 i=0; d2 s=0, followed by L1: d3 s=s+i; d4 i=i+1. L1 can repeat itself or exit to L2: return s. The loop body generates d3,d4 and kills d1,d2. Its self edge lets its own definitions reach its next entry.

Reaching definitions for the loop, each cell is IN / OUT
RoundL0L1L2
0{} / {}{} / {}{} / {}
1{} / {d1,d2}{} / {d3,d4}{} / {}
2{} / {d1,d2}{d1,d2,d3,d4} / {d3,d4}{d3,d4} / {d3,d4}
3{} / {d1,d2}{d1,d2,d3,d4} / {d3,d4}{d3,d4} / {d3,d4}

At L1 entry, the initial definitions can arrive on the first iteration and the body definitions can arrive on a later iteration. A single forward textual pass that ignores the back edge misses the second possibility. Fixed-point iteration combines both without enumerating every iteration count.

practice.title: Verify stability
practice.statementHtml: Substitute the final diamond sets into the equations at B3 for reaching definitions and B1 for liveness.
hints: Recompute rather than assuming the final row is stable.
practice.answerHtml:
To verify a final table, recompute every IN from its graph neighbours and every OUT from its local transfer, or reverse those roles for liveness. Check the boundary separately. A table is not justified by the words no change unless the displayed sets actually satisfy all equations.

For B3 in the diamond, union({d2,d3},{d1,d4}) gives {d1,d2,d3,d4}. Adding GEN {d5} with no kills gives its displayed OUT. For liveness at B1, OUT {x,y} minus DEF {x} leaves {y}; union USE {y} still gives {y}. These small substitutions connect the equations to the completed tables.

quiz.prompt: Which neighbours supply IN for reaching definitions?
quiz.explanation: Definitions flow forward along incoming graph edges.

quiz.prompt: Which neighbours supply OUT for live variables?
quiz.explanation: Future needs travel backward from successor entries.

quiz.prompt: What does KILL contain for a block assigning x?
options: Other definitions of x overwritten by the block
quiz.explanation: Assigning x prevents earlier definitions of x from surviving through the block.

quiz.prompt: Why is z absent from USE of z=x+y; return z?
options: z is defined before its read
quiz.explanation: USE describes incoming values needed before a local definition.

quiz.prompt: What merge operation do these two may analyses use?
quiz.explanation: A possibility on any relevant path must be retained.

quiz.prompt: Why does the reaching-definition universe need definition labels?
options: Different assignments to one name must stay distinct
quiz.explanation: Origin information distinguishes x's earlier and later assignments.

quiz.prompt: What makes the bottom-up iteration terminate here?
options: Finite fact universe and monotone updates
quiz.explanation: Facts cannot grow indefinitely in a finite lattice.

quiz.prompt: When OUT changes in a forward worklist, which blocks need scheduling?
quiz.explanation: Successor IN values depend on that changed OUT.

quiz.prompt: At diamond B3 entry, which x definitions may reach?
quiz.explanation: B2 preserves d1, while B1 produces d3.

quiz.prompt: Does a may fact prove a path executes for some actual input?
options: Only if the set is sorted
quiz.explanation: The graph can conservatively include infeasible paths.

quiz.prompt: What is the correct fixed-point stopping condition?
quiz.explanation: Neighbour propagation must stabilise throughout the graph.

keyPoints.en: Reaching definitions propagates possible assignment origins forward.
keyPoints.bn: কোন অ্যাসাইনমেন্টের মান আসতে পারে, তা সামনের ব্লকে পাঠাও।

keyPoints.en: Live variables propagates possible future needs backward.
keyPoints.bn: পরে কোন ভেরিয়েবলের মান লাগবে, সে খবর পেছনের ব্লকে পাঠাও।

keyPoints.en: USE contains reads before a local definition.
keyPoints.bn: ব্লকের ভেতরে মান দেওয়ার আগেই যা পড়তে হয়, সেটিই USE-এ রাখো।

keyPoints.en: A fixed point satisfies every transfer and merge equation.
keyPoints.bn: সব সেটের আপডেটে আর পরিবর্তন না এলে fixed point পাওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: May analysis can include paths that never execute for real inputs.
keyPoints.bn: বাস্তবে না-চলা পথের সম্ভাবনাও may analysis-এর সেটে থাকতে পারে।
